title: Golden-state reconciler and soft-swap recovery plans for safe config applies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Config rollouts for batching, KV cache, and kernel scheduling occasionally cause subtle divergence between in-memory runtime state and the control-plane view (prefix warming, stale routing, mis-sized batch windows), which can spike token costs or increase tail latency. Existing rollback triggers are noisy or too aggressive and do not provide a deterministic recovery plan.

Proposal: Implement a Golden-State Reconciler that maintains a lightweight, canonical snapshot of runtime-safe config invariants (batch windows, cache warming state, prefix quarantine markers) and supports a soft-swap apply mode plus an executable Recovery Plan when a failure trigger fires. Goals: reduce false-positive rollbacks, automate safe recovery, and provide operator-friendly explanation and manual override. Integrate synthetic probing (traffic canary), cost-aware cooldown heuristics, and persisted recovery plans that survive restarts.

Scope: reconciler service, soft-swap apply flow, synthetic probe runner, recovery plan DSL, operator UI hooks (Console), telemetry and audit events for every state transition.
acceptance_criteria: Golden-State Reconciler exposes a /reconcile API and stores a canonical runtime snapshot for a config target
Soft-swap applies stage config changes into a shadow runtime and only promote when synthetic probes and KV-prefix warmup signals pass
Recovery Plan is auto-generated on failure and includes an ordered set of rollback or remedial steps plus estimated cost impact
Trigger rules include economic cooldown (avoids rollbacks for temporary cost spikes) and a confidence score to avoid noisy flips
All state transitions emit structured audit events compatible with Console and exports to existing telemetry pipeline
Manual operator approval path in Console that shows diff, probe results, and one-click revert to golden state
design_decisions: Maintain only lightweight invariants in Golden-State (no full model KV dumps) to keep storage small and reconciliation fast
Soft-swap promotes after a minimum of N successful synthetic probes and sustained latency/cost within thresholds
Use a declarative Recovery Plan DSL (steps: quiesce, prefix-quarantine, staged-warmup, promote, rollback-if) to keep plans replayable
Keep economic cooldown logic conservative: require sustained deviation for > T seconds before triggering automatic rollback
Persist Recovery Plans to distributed KV with versioning so plans are inspectable and can be audited post-incident
implementation_steps: Spec: API + Recovery Plan DSL (Confluence doc) and telemetry contract
Service: implement golden-state reconciler service with snapshot store and /reconcile endpoint
Soft-swap flow: change-applier accepts 'soft' flag and creates shadow config, routes 2% synthetic probes
Synthetic probes: lightweight probe harness that replays representative prefixes and measures latency/cost signals
Recovery plan generator: algorithm that selects remediation steps and cost delta estimate
Console: UI surface to visualize golden vs candidate state, probe results, and approve/revert
Integrations: wire audit events to logging pipeline and alerts for confidence < 0.6
E2E tests: simulate config regression, validate that recovery plan executes and returns to golden state
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic probes may not cover real traffic patterns -> Mitigation: allow customer-provided probe sets and sample production traces in shadow mode
Risk: Added control-plane latency for reconciler -> Mitigation: keep reconciler async; soft-swap promotes via heartbeat not blocking applies
Risk: Recovery plan mis-executes in edge cases -> Mitigation: require canary stage with manual approval for high-impact targets and add simulated dry-run
Risk: Storage bloat from snapshots -> Mitigation: compress snapshots, keep N=3 latest per target, expire per retention policy
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial spec drafted in Confluence (link below). Scoped acceptance criteria with PM and SRE.
2026-03-05: Spike complete for synthetic-probe harness; baseline latency/variance numbers collected against canary model.
2026-03-08: Early reconciler PoC stores snapshots in blobstore; showed 40ms median reconcile time for single target.
2026-03-10: Design review with Console team — decided to add an 'operator-review' gate for Dedicated targets.
2026-03-12: Implementing Recovery Plan DSL parser and initial generator heuristics (work in progress).
2026-03-13: PR opened for probe harness: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4201 (needs tests + perf guardrails)
qa_and_rollout_plan: Start in internal staging with non-customer traffic and run soft-swap on low-risk targets
Run shadow mode for 48h on 5% of production routes, collect probe-based metrics and false-positive rate
Enable automatic rollback only for test orgs; require manual approval for Dedicated/Private until 2 weeks of stable metrics
Post-rollout: monitor cost delta, rollback frequency, and operator interventions for 30 days
notes: This ticket intentionally separates the reconciler (state + snapshot) from the executor (apply/rollback runner). Keep the reconciler read-only for decisioning and have a small, verified executor binary handle live mutations. We prioritize predictable, auditable state transitions over 'clever' heuristics that are hard to reason about. Follow-up work: expose recovery plan simulation in CI for PRs that change batching/cache defaults. PM feedback: must include clear SLA language for Dedicated customers when soft-swap defers promotion.
